newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian shares soar on new money, seen rising more.
newsitem.headline: Russian shares soar on new money, seen rising more.

text.p: Leading Russian shares soared on Wednesday in record-high volume on new money flowing into the market on positive political and economic news, traders said.
They forecast a further rise in the next few days.
The Russian Trading System index of 24 shares rose by 6.91 percent to 181.64 on a massive $46.97 million in volume.

Prices soared in the morning to stabilise on some profit-taking from Russian brokers in the afternoon and edged up some more in the evening, said Alexei Genkin, manager of international sales at IK Aton.
"After the credit rating investors have re-evaluated Russia to the better," he said. "The market has already discounted Yeltsin's health and any possible political turmoil."
He said the better-than-expected ratings and news that President Boris Yeltsin had moved from hospital where he was getting ready for his heart operation to a sanatorium pushed prices up.

"Everything coincided very favourably -- both ratings and price levels and the news about Gazprom and the information about Boris Yeltsin's preparation for the operation," said Andrei Galperin, a trader from Creditanstalt-Grant.
On Monday Gazprom announced the preliminary price of $14-16 for its placement of American Depositary Shares, each equivalent to 10 ordinary shares.
Gazprom was traded at $0.461 after $0.430 at Tuesday's close.
Genkin forecast the market would rise for the next few days, pushed further up by news the International Monetary Fund released a new tranche of its $10 million to Russia.
The news came after trading was over.
St Petersburg Telephone rose to $0.83 from $0.74, UES was traded at $0.0805 after $0.0755, LUkoil rose to $10.10 from $9.85 and Mosenergo was $1.000 after $0.945.
